niche: a bank research desk's call, sent at 18:00 the evening before to its markets floor and its clients, on a statistics office's advance estimate of June-quarter real GDP growth at an annual rate, built the day after a monthly trade and business stocks bulletin, delayed by a systems outage, gave wholesalers', retailers' and manufacturers' June stocks at book value, with import prices having risen in two legs, in March and in June
answer: 2.8 per cent: real GDP growth in the June quarter 2026 at a compound annual rate, as the Statistics Office's advance estimate of 30 July 2026 will show it (0.69 per cent on the March quarter)
stakeholder_role: a commercial bank's research desk economist who files the desk's call on the advance GDP estimate to clients at 18:00 the evening before the release

spine.entity: one month's merchandise exports or imports with one partner country in one SITC division, as the trade and business statistics unit's bulk download carries it
spine.grain: flow x partner country x SITC division x month

world.geography: a fictional English-speaking country of about 7 million with its own dollar (its statistics office, trade and business statistics unit, reserve bank, bank, poll and people are fictional; personas on the British index)

driver: The decisive quantity is the change over a period in the volume of a stock that each holder reports at what it paid, and because a holder's stock on any date was bought over a holding period of its own, the reported value mixes the prices of the weeks the goods were bought in; read at the reporting month's price, the textbook removal of price gains, a price step inside the holding period reads as a fall in volume, read at the period's average price it reads the other way, and only revaluing each holder's stock at the average price over its own holding period, at both ends of the period, separates volume from price.
driver_concrete: Each industry's end-March and end-June book-value stocks (wholesale, retail and manufacturing, from the trade and business stocks bulletin) are revalued at the average of the industry's input price index over the months its stock-to-sales ratio covers before the change in inventory volume is taken, because import prices rose in March and again in June and the stock on hand at each quarter end was partly bought before each rise; deflating at the quarter end's own price index understates the volume at both quarter ends, the June one by more because the larger leg sits inside its holding period, so the quarter reads as a deeper run-down (2.2 against 2.8), and deflating at the quarter's average price reads it the other way (3.3).
stump: A strong analyst who takes the desk's track for every line the late bulletin does not feed, builds goods exports and imports from the bulletin section by section and deflates each industry's end-March and end-June book-value stocks by that month's price index, the textbook removal of holding gains, files 2.2 per cent against the golden 2.8, because the June leg of the import price rise reads as a fall in the volume of stocks that were bought before it.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who takes the desk's track for every line the late bulletin does not feed, reads the bulletin's book-value stocks and the user guide's volume definition correctly and deflates each industry's end-March and end-June stock by that month's price index files 2.2 per cent, six tenths under the golden 2.8; deflating at each quarter's average price files 3.3, a two-month holding period for every industry 3.1, revaluing only the June end 3.3, and only revaluing each stock at its industry's prices over the months its stock-to-sales ratio covers, at both quarter ends, files the golden (executed on the generator's clean truth, checks.py R3a and R3b).
domain_test: The call turns on the volume of business inventory investment in the advance estimate, which national accountants measure by revaluing book-value stocks at the prices of the weeks the goods were bought in over each industry's turnover period (the turnover method behind the inventory valuation adjustment) before differencing; with a hospital's nouns there is no book-valued stock turning over at cost, no producer price path and no annualised volume aggregate built from expenditure lines, so the task stops reading.

each release in the real-time database at its own reference year's prices
the desk's 26 June download of the real-time database against the annual national accounts of 21 July

notes: Stump strategy time_semantics (relabelled at stage 3 from decomposition_attribution, which guard.py heart blocked against task152 and task234 v2): the step a solver misses is the effective dating of the prices a book value carries, each industry's purchases spread over its own holding period rather than the reporting month's prices; once the dating is right the volume-price split follows. The strategy's WARN (time semantics often decides on a field read or a stated rule) is answered: no field, code or filed rule dates the purchases; the bulletin's 'Stocks are at cost' is read correctly by the default path, the window is modelled from each industry's stock-to-sales ratio and validated against the Office's estimates of 28 past quarters (RMSE $9.9m against $33.6m and more for every rival), and checks.py R3a and R3b execute the analyst test on the clean truth. Gate G method_or_model_selection (relabelled from decomposition_attribution): several defensible revaluations of a book value, the right one pinned by validation against the realised outcomes and by the 2008 SNA the user guide cites. G1 first: the book value's unit of value (cost at purchase) is not the period's prices the volume needs. Redrawn after the DRAWN pull brought task153 (registered an hour earlier): calibration pilot_log -> realised_outcome_roster (the method is validated against the Office's own estimates of past quarters' change in business inventories, the realised outcomes, reconstructed from TBS's history; no desk pilot log ships) and forum customer_or_counterparty -> operations_desk (at 18:00 the call goes to Tarbert's markets floor, whose rates and currency desks position for the release on it, as well as to clients in the evening preview).
